title: Correct fragment-level token accounting for interleaved audio->text streaming sessions
creator: Asha Rao
description:
Summary: Some customers using live audio transcription + incremental patching are seeing double-charges or lost input credit when clients send interleaved partial transcripts and later patch them (replace/overwrite fragments). This ticket stabilizes fragment attribution semantics in the metering pipeline so that token counts are deterministic and robust to out-of-order/overwrite fragment events.

Context: We support an audio->text streaming mode where clients send partial hypotheses and then a final transcript or delta edits. The front-end streaming service currently emits metering events based on fragment arrival and a best-effort merge step; however, when fragments are replaced or re-ordered (client resyncs, network duplicates), we observed two failure modes: (A) orphaned provisional credits that were never debited when a fragment was later overwritten causing undercharging; (B) duplicate debit when a resumed stream replays a previous fragment and the pipeline treats it as new. Both lead to customer confusion and either lost revenue or incorrect refunds.

Goal: Implement deterministic fragment lifecycle states in the metering pipeline and an idempotent reconciliation pass that (1) tracks fragment IDs, sequence numbers, and canonical boundaries, (2) computes deltas to committed token tallies when fragments are replaced or removed, and (3) emits single-source-of-truth ledger events consumed by billing and quota systems.
investigation_notes: 11/12: Reproduced locally with synthetic client that sends partial hypotheses then 'replace' patches. Observed mismatch between front-end provisional ledger and final batchizer emissions.
11/13: Heap of logs show fragment UUIDs are not surface-preserved across edge proxies; proxy sometimes assigns a new id on reconnect leading to duplicate accounting.

11/14: Tokenizer differences between preliminary hypothesis (client-side V1 tokenizer) and server-side canonical tokenizer cause token_count drift on replacement. Drift leads to reconciliation complexity.

11/16: Found race in metering-aggregator where 'finalize_fragment' and 'replace_fragment' updates interleave and both trigger debit events. Root causes: missing fragment version, lack of canonicalization, and non-idempotent debit function.
11/18: Cross-checked with ENG-754321 (attachment-aware normalization) for shared heuristics; some ideas reusable.
11/19: Product confirmed >2 enterprise incidents in last quarter complaining about 'chat credits disappearing' during live captioning demos.
repro_steps: Run local streaming test harness: start frontend proxy with simulated unstable network (reconnects enabled).
Client stream flow: send partial fragment A (hypothesis 1), send partial fragment B (hypothesis 2, overwrite A), then send final fragment C (finalized).
Force a proxy reconnect to cause fragment UUID reassignment and replay partials, then observe metering events in /metrics/metering-log and compare provisional vs committed tallies.
Observe duplicate debit events or missing debit for replaced fragments by querying staging billing ledger (staging-ledger.redwood.internal).
proposed_changes: Introduce fragment canonicalization: front-end should attach client-provided fragment_id if present; proxy must preserve fragment_id or map to stable id anchored to session + seq. Add backpointer header when id remapping occurs.
Add fragment lifecycle states in metering-aggregator: PROVISIONAL -> COMMITTED -> REPLACED -> CANCELLED. Each state transition must be idempotent and emit a single delta event for ledger consumption.

Implement server-side canonical tokenization: compute server_token_count and include it in fragment metadata for reconciliation; store original raw bytes for re-tokenization if patch differences occur.
Change debit flow to be delta-based: on REPLACED, compute delta = tokens(new) - tokens(old) and emit a single credit/debit event reflecting only the delta, not the absolute values.
Persist fragment version vector (fragment_id + version++) in the metering store with TTL aligned to session retention to support late reconciliations.
Make billing consumer idempotent: ledger event includes fragment_id and event_uuid; consumer ignores duplicate event_uuid and can rollback using fragment version if necessary.
Add migration tool to backfill fragment_id mapping for impacted sessions in the last 90 days for accounts with incidents (limited-scoped run before rollout).
rollout_plan: Dev: implement canonicalization and delta debit logic behind feature flag (metering.fragment-delta-v1).
Staging: run end-to-end harness with fuzzed reconnects and third-party client simulators for 72h; validate ledger parity and per-session invariants.
Canary: enable feature for 5% of traffic (non-enterprise), monitor for billing/latency regressions for 48h.
Enterprise Gradual: enable for 3 pilot enterprise accounts known to have reported issues and work closely with customer success for verification.
Full rollout: after 7 days of healthy canary, enable globally and disable old code path. Run backfill migrations as necessary.
Fallback: if regressions appear, flip feature flag off to restore previous behavior while debugging.
Post-rollout: run reconciliation report comparing pre/post token tallies for 30 days for sampled sessions.
monitoring: Add histogram: metering.delta_tokens_per_replace to track distribution of deltas emitted on REPLACED events.
Add counter: metering.duplicate_debit_detected with tags (account, region) to surface idempotency failures.
Add alert: if duplicate_debit_detected > 5/min for >10 minutes for canary, page SRE and revert feature flag.
Dashboard: session-level ledger parity view (provisional vs committed) with ability to drill to fragment-level events.
SLO: ensure median metering pipeline tail latency increase < 10ms after change; track 99th percentile for billing consumer pipeline.
Privacy: ensure logs scrub raw audio bytes; store only minimal bounding info for debugging.
qa_test_plan: Automated: unit tests for lifecycle transitions and delta generation; fuzz tests that randomize reorder/replace/cancel sequences and assert ledger invariants.
Integration: end-to-end test with staging billing consumer and simulated client resends.
Manual: replay two customer incidents from production snapshots in a sandbox and verify corrected ledger outcomes.
Edge-cases: test tokenization drift scenarios where client and server tokenizers disagree; ensure delta logic reconciles without double charge.
Load: run on staging at 2x production streaming concurrency to ensure no performance regression.
